statements.t: We expect that future direct and indirect sales to Nokia, KYEC and Cadence Design Systems will continue to fluctuate significantly on a quarterly basis.

The networking and telecommunications market has accounted for a significant portion of our net revenues in the past and has declined during the past several years and is expected to continue to decline.
In May 2026, we announced that we were awarded Phase I of a Smart City project by a local government agency in Taiwan named the Smart Guardian Eye project.

In October 2026, we successfully completed, and the Hsinchu County government in Taiwan accepted, the initial stage of Phase I of the Smart Guardian Eye project, which is now providing live AI video monitoring and interpretive incident reporting.
We intend to submit our proposal for Phase II of the Smart Guardian Eye project during the remainder of fiscal 2027.
Pursuant to an agreed-upon schedule, we will receive milestone payments which total an estimated $2.0 million upon successful completion of each milestone.

Development of our next-generation Plato processor remains on schedule for a March 2027 tape-out, with first-spin chips targeted for initial sampling by late summer of calendar 2027, and we continue to receive outside interest based on the disclosed preliminary performance and power savings findings.

Our software development team is conducting an internal trial and validation of the alpha version of the SDK, and we anticipate releasing the alpha version to our initial customers before the end of December 2026, with a commercial release targeted for the first half of calendar 2027.

The SDK is an important step in our commercialization strategy to make the Gemini-II architecture accessible to a broader developer ecosystem and is expected to enable prospective customers and partners to evaluate our technology using their own AI models, support multiple simultaneous evaluations, accelerate software development, simplify application deployment and provide a foundation for working with a broader…

We believe that during the next 12 months, continued inflationary pressures, increased or new tariffs, export controls and other trade barriers, trade disputes, and increasing geopolitical tensions will continue to negatively impact general economic activity and demand in our end markets.

Although it is difficult to estimate the length or severity of these conditions, we expect them to have an adverse effect on our results of operations, financial position, including potential impairments, and liquidity through the remainder of fiscal 2027 and beyond.

We also sell our products to OEMs that manufacture products for military and aerospace applications such as radar and guidance systems, missiles and satellites, for test and measurement applications such as high-speed testers, for automotive applications such as smart cruise control, and for medical applications such as ultrasound and CAT scan equipment.

If prices decline, our ability to increase net revenues, therefore, is dependent upon our ability to increase unit sales volumes of existing products and to introduce and sell new products with higher average selling prices in quantities sufficient to compensate for the anticipated declines in selling prices of our more mature products.
Furthermore, our customers may delay scheduled delivery dates and/or cancel orders within specified timeframes without significant penalty.
Thus, we will recognize revenue upon shipment of the product for direct sales and sales to our distributors.

Our revenues have been substantially impacted by significant fluctuations in sales to Nokia, KYEC and Cadence Design Systems, and we expect that future direct and indirect sales to Nokia, KYEC and Cadence Design Systems will continue to fluctuate substantially on a quarterly basis and that such fluctuations may significantly affect our operating results in future periods.

We expect that our overall gross margins will fluctuate from period to period as a result of shifts in product mix, changes in average selling prices and our ability to control our cost of revenues, including costs associated with outsourced wafer fabrication and product assembly and testing.
We believe that continued investment in research and development is critical to our long-term success, and we expect to continue to devote significant resources to product development activities.

Accordingly, we expect that our research and development expenses will increase in future periods as we expand our hardware and software development teams to commercialize our Gemini-II product offerings and develop Plato product offerings.

We expect that our sales and marketing expenses will increase in absolute dollars in future periods if we are able to grow and expand our sales force but that, to the extent our revenues increase in future periods, these expenses will generally decline as a percentage of net revenues.
We also expect that, in support of any future growth that we are able to achieve, general and administrative expenses will generally increase in absolute dollars.
We expect these higher manufacturing costs to continue for the foreseeable future.

We are currently reviewing our manufacturing costs and intend to pass on any cost increases to our customers when it makes sense to do so; however, to the extent we are unable to increase the selling prices of our products sufficiently to offset these higher costs, our gross profit and gross margin may continue to be adversely affected.

The increase in research and development spending was primarily related to increases of $1.5 million in outside design consulting expenses for our Plato project, $736,000 in payroll related expenses and $104,000 in stock-based compensation.
We expect external design services for Plato to continue until the completion of the Plato tape-out.

The increase in research and development spending was primarily related to increases of $2.6 million in outside design consulting expenses for our Plato project, $1.7 million in payroll related expenses and $426,000 in stock-based compensation expense.
We do not expect to incur significant additional expenses related to these matters.

We expect that we may continue to carry higher levels of inventory for the foreseeable future in order to mitigate the risk of supply disruptions and meet customer delivery commitments in light of these industry-wide constraints.
We cannot assure you that additional equity financing or debt financing, if required, will be available on terms that are acceptable or at all.

estimates.t: Our critical accounting estimates are disclosed in our Annual Report on Form 10-K for the fiscal year ended March 31, 2026.

statements.t: Lee-Lean Shu, Chairman and Chief Executive Officer, stated, “In the second quarter of fiscal 2027, we made significant progress on several fronts, including the successful completion and acceptance of the initial stage of Phase I of our Smart Guardian Eye project, which is now providing live video monitoring and interpretive incident reporting.
We anticipate releasing a beta version to our initial customers before the end of December 2026.

Shu continued, "Looking ahead to the remainder of fiscal 2027, we are focused on achieving the following milestones: submitting our proposal for Phase II of the Smart Guardian Eye project, advancing the AI-assisted SDK toward commercial release in the first half of calendar year 2027, completing the tape-out of Plato in March 2027, with first-spin chips targeted for initial sampling by late summer of calendar…
“To address higher manufacturing costs, the Company plans to implement price increases immediately for new orders and effective January 1, 2027, for existing customer backlog.

Management anticipates that these adjustments, together with improved product availability, will support a recovery in revenue and gross margin beginning in the fourth quarter of fiscal 2027,” concluded Mr.
Net revenues were within the Company’s guidance range of $5.7 million to $6.5 million.

Gross margin was below the Company’s guidance of approximately 53% to 55%, and decreased year-over-year, primarily due to an unfavorable product mix and higher manufacturing costs resulting from supply chain constraints for wafers and outsourced assembly, burn-in and test operations.
We are currently reviewing our manufacturing costs and intend to pass on any cost increases to our customers when it makes sense to do so.

The year-over-year increase in research and development expenses during the second quarter of fiscal 2027 was driven primarily by external design services related to the development of our next-generation Plato processor, which are expected to continue until the completion of the Plato tape-out in March 2027.
We do not expect to incur significant additional expenses related to these matters.

Management will conduct a conference call to review the Company's financial results for the second quarter of fiscal year 2027, and its current outlook for the third quarter of fiscal 2027 at 1:30 p.m.
A webcast of the call will be archived on the Company’s investor relations website under the Events and Presentations tab.
